workflow_sequence.description: EddInputReceived: the requester provides a portable EddRefinementInput document. The CLI parses the document, including the raw `modification_scope` list, and passes it to the workflow along with an input anchor path.

TargetRepositoryPreflight: the workflow invokes the preflight Activity. The target Git worktree and starting revision are resolved, and the raw `modification_scope` entries are confirmed to exist inside the repo root, but the resolved list is not yet attached to the context.

RunInitialized: `InitializeRunActivity` derives the run id, creates or resumes the v5 progress record, and resolves the raw `modification_scope` to a canonical list of repo-relative, POSIX-style paths (appending a trailing slash for existing directories). The canonical list is persisted under `record['modification_scope']` so fresh and resumed runs use the same value.

handshake_points.data_shape: {run_id, schema_version: 5, modification_scope: list[string], starting_revision, best_accepted_state: null, ...}

workflow_sequence.description: RefinementPlanned: `EddPlanRunner` reads the `edd-plan` skill's `plan.json`, then validates every entry in `plan['intended_files']` against the persisted `modification_scope` using `PathScopeChecker`. If all intended files are authorized, the planning result proceeds as before.

PlanScopeRejected: when one or more `intended_files` fall outside the authorized scope, `EddPlanRunner` short-circuits without invoking `edd_do`. It returns a `PlanningResult` carrying `rejection_reason: 'plan_out_of_scope'`, the offending action/rationale/evidence, and the offending paths. No candidate is created.

handshake_points.data_shape: {rejection_reason: 'plan_out_of_scope', out_of_scope_details: {offending_action, rationale, evidence, paths}, stop_recommendation: true}

workflow_sequence.description: RefinementExecuted: for an in-scope plan, the workflow invokes `edd_do`. The activity runs the selected action through `DevinHarness` and measures the real diff (`git diff --name-only`) and a canonical diff hash, returning an `ExecutionResult`.

handshake_points.data_shape: {target_context, action, intended_files, accept_edits_config} -> {changed_files: list[string], diff_hash, usage_metrics}

workflow_sequence.description: CandidateValidated: `validate_candidate` receives the `PlanningResult` (which now includes `modification_scope`), the `ExecutionResult`, and the approved diff hash. It checks `changed_files` against `modification_scope` first, then against `intended_files`, returning distinguishable rejection reasons.

handshake_points.data_shape: {run_id, planning: {modification_scope, intended_files}, execution: ExecutionResult, approved_diff_hash, repo_root} -> CandidateValidationResult

workflow_sequence.description: DiffScopeRejected: when a changed file is outside `modification_scope`, `validate_candidate` returns a `CandidateValidationResult` with `rejection_reason: 'diff_out_of_scope'` and the offending paths. The candidate is persisted but marked as rejected.

OutOfScopeAlarmed: the workflow inspects `PlanningResult.rejection_reason` and `CandidateValidationResult.rejection_reason`. On `plan_out_of_scope` or `diff_out_of_scope`, it raises `OutOfScopeModificationError` with a structured `out_of_scope_details` payload instead of quietly returning.

RunFinalized: the exception-driven finalize path in `EddRefinementWorkflow.run` catches `OutOfScopeModificationError`, invokes `finalize_run` with `terminal_reason='out_of_scope_modification'`, releases the mutation lease, and writes a terminal report. `FinalizeRunActivity` resets the worktree to `starting_revision` when no `best_accepted_state` exists, or to the accepted commit otherwise, and continues even if the git reset fails.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when `InitializeRunActivity` resolves and canonicalizes the authorized modification scope from the input document.

data_points.description: Number of canonical scope entries persisted.
Path to the EddRefinementInput document for traceability.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when `EddPlanRunner` rejects a plan because one or more intended files are outside the authorized scope.

data_points.description: The intended file paths that failed scope containment.
The plan's own stated rationale for the action.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when `validate_candidate` finds a changed file outside the authorized modification scope.

data_points.description: Stable identifier for the offending candidate.
The actual diff paths that failed scope containment.
The canonical modification_scope used for the check.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when the workflow raises `OutOfScopeModificationError` to trigger the exception-driven finalize path.

data_points.description: Whether the violation was detected at 'plan' or 'diff' time.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when `FinalizeRunActivity` attempts to restore the worktree to a clean starting or accepted revision.

data_points.description: Whether the git reset completed without error.

instrumentation_events.description: Emitted when `FinalizeRunActivity` releases the repository-scoped mutation lease, either on a normal terminal path or after an out-of-scope exception.

data_points.description: The terminal reason passed to finalize_run.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Resolve and persist the canonical `modification_scope` in `InitializeRunActivity`.
new_responsibilities.intent: The workflow layer is where the input document first meets the target repository; it owns the transformation from raw input to durable, repo-relative scope.
Defensive, deterministic gating of the planning output must live outside the agentic skill (ADR-017).
The real diff is the ground truth for unauthorized writes; the backend is the only layer that can compare it to the persisted authorized scope.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Raise `OutOfScopeModificationError` from the workflow on a confirmed plan-time or diff-time violation.
new_responsibilities.intent: Only the orchestration layer has enough context to turn an activity-level rejection into a terminal, lease-releasing stop.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Route out-of-scope stops to `finalize_run` with the distinct `terminal_reason` `out_of_scope_modification`.
new_responsibilities.intent: Reuses ADR-023's exception-driven finalize path instead of duplicating lease-release logic.
A single, filesystem-agnostic helper guarantees the same semantics at plan time and diff time.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Distinguish exact-file scope entries from directory prefixes using a trailing-slash convention and `PurePosixPath` containment.
new_responsibilities.intent: Naive string prefixing would allow `foo-bar/x` to match a `foo/` scope; the helper prevents this.
Durable state is the only source of truth that survives worker restarts and resumed runs.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Update `ProgressRecordSerializer.for_v5` to allow `modification_scope` and `scope_violations` through redaction.
new_responsibilities.intent: A future round-trip save/load path must not silently drop these fields.

new_responsibilities.responsibility: Persist a terminal report with the `out_of_scope_modification` reason and the captured violation details.
new_responsibilities.intent: The terminal report is the durable, human-readable record of why the run ended.

contracts.name: ProgressRecordV5
contracts.description: The durable run record now carries the authorized modification scope and any scope violations that occur during the run.

changes.added: `modification_scope` (list of repo-relative POSIX path strings) and `scope_violations` (list of {check, paths, action, rationale, evidence}) fields.

contracts.name: PlanningResult
contracts.description: The planning result now threads the authorized scope and can report a plan-time scope rejection without invoking `edd_do`.

changes.added: `modification_scope` (canonical scope used for the check), `rejection_reason` (e.g. 'plan_out_of_scope'), and `out_of_scope_details` (offending action/rationale/evidence/paths).
changes.modified: `EddPlanRunner.run` short-circuits to a `stop_recommendation` result when `intended_files` contains out-of-scope paths; `action` may be 'stop' with a diagnostic payload.

contracts.name: CandidateValidationResult
contracts.description: Validation now distinguishes an unauthorized file diff from a deviation between the actual diff and the plan's intended files.

changes.modified: `ValidateCandidateActivity.run` checks `changed_files` against `planning['modification_scope']` before the existing `intended_files` check. The existing `out_of_scope` reason is retained for unplanned (but authorized-scope) changes.

contracts.name: PathScopeChecker
contracts.description: A shared utility contract for checking whether a repo-relative candidate path is inside an authorized scope list.

changes.added: `PathScopeChecker.is_authorized(candidate: str, scope: list[str]) -> bool` with exact-file and directory-prefix semantics based on `PurePosixPath`.

contracts.name: OutOfScopeWorkflowError
contracts.description: A dedicated exception type carries a structured out-of-scope payload from the workflow into the exception-driven finalize path.

changes.modified: `EddRefinementWorkflow.run` catches `OutOfScopeModificationError` and calls `finalize_run` with the exception's terminal reason before re-raising, similar to the generic exception path in ADR-023.

contracts.name: FinalizeRunCleanup
contracts.description: Finalization now guarantees a clean worktree on any terminal path that lacks an accepted candidate, and does not lose the terminal report if git reset fails.

changes.added: `FinalizeRunActivity.run` restores to `record['starting_revision']` when `best_accepted_state` is None; git reset failures are logged and swallowed so the terminal report is still written and the lease released.
changes.modified: The terminal report includes `scope_violations` when present.

architectural_decisions.decision: Persist `modification_scope` in the v5 `ProgressRecord` and read it from the record in `edd_plan` and `validate_candidate`, not from the original CLI input.
architectural_decisions.justification: This makes the authorized scope a durable, single source of truth that is identical for fresh and resumed runs, matching the `iteration_start_baseline` threading pattern already in use.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How is the authorized scope threaded to resumed runs?

architectural_decisions.decision: Implement a single `PathScopeChecker` in `common/scoped_path_validator.py` using `PurePosixPath` and a trailing-slash directory/exact-file discriminator.
architectural_decisions.justification: A shared, filesystem-agnostic helper guarantees that plan-time and diff-time containment checks never drift. `PurePosixPath` avoids naive string-prefix bugs such as `foo-bar/x` matching `foo/`.
architectural_decisions.basis: requirements.md Requirement 2; existing `common/scoped_path_validator.py` is the base primitive.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How is path containment checked without false positives?

architectural_decisions.decision: Report plan-time and diff-time out-of-scope detections as structured `PlanningResult` and `CandidateValidationResult` values, then raise `OutOfScopeModificationError` from the workflow.
architectural_decisions.justification: Activities remain deterministic and easy to unit test; the orchestration layer makes the terminal-halt decision. This also lets the existing `try/except` in `EddRefinementWorkflow.run` handle finalization.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How does an out-of-scope detection become a hard stop?

architectural_decisions.decision: Reuse the existing exception-driven finalize path in `EddRefinementWorkflow.run` for out-of-scope stops rather than adding a special-case finalize branch.
architectural_decisions.justification: ADR-023 already guarantees mutation lease release and terminal report on unhandled exceptions. Raising a dedicated exception preserves this invariant without duplicating cleanup logic.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How is the lease released on an out-of-scope stop?

architectural_decisions.decision: Do not count an out-of-scope stop toward `consecutive_confirmed_regressions` or any iteration/token budget.
architectural_decisions.justification: An out-of-scope write is an authorization/control failure, not a measured quality regression. Conflating the two would allow a small number of tolerated 'regressions' to mask a security-relevant scope breach.
architectural_decisions.basis: requirements.md open question 1; ADR-017 (regression is a quality-measurement concept).
architectural_decisions.impact: `EddRefinementWorkflow` and `FinalizeRunActivity` treat `out_of_scope_modification` as an immediate, independent terminal reason.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should a confirmed out-of-scope stop count toward consecutive_confirmed_regressions or any existing budget counter?

architectural_decisions.decision: Add a dedicated `scope_violations` list to the `ProgressRecord` and terminal report, parallel to `regression_evidence` and `reverted_proposals`.
architectural_decisions.justification: Scope violations are rare but critical control events. A durable, structured list supports observability, post-mortems, and future cross-run aggregation without overloading the existing `candidate_history` or `rejected_or_reverted_summaries` fields.
architectural_decisions.basis: requirements.md Requirement 5 (diagnostic payload); ProgressRecord v5 already uses durable evidence lists.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Do we want a dedicated scope_violations list in the progress record / terminal report for observability?

architectural_decisions.decision: Canonicalize `modification_scope` in `InitializeRunActivity` (repo-relative POSIX, trailing slash for existing directories) and let the `PathScopeChecker` treat a trailing slash as the directory/exact-file discriminator.
architectural_decisions.justification: This keeps the containment helper pure and fast, makes the persisted scope canonical for resumption, and still allows the helper to reject sibling-prefix matches.
architectural_decisions.basis: requirements.md Requirement 1 and open question 4; common/scoped_path_validator.py.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should trailing-slash normalization for directory scope entries be enforced at EddRefinementInput parse time or handled defensively in the containment helper?

architectural_decisions.decision: Deliver the scope persistence, plan-time check, diff-time check, and cleanup as one cohesive multi-activity change rather than two vertical slices.
architectural_decisions.justification: The four capabilities are tightly coupled: without persistence the checks cannot survive resumption, without the hard stop the cleanup is not triggered, and without cleanup the breach persists. A single coherent change keeps the invariants intact.
architectural_decisions.impact: All touched activities and the workflow are updated and tested together.
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should this work be delivered as two vertical slices or as one cohesive multi-activity change?

questions_addressed.question: Should a confirmed out-of-scope stop count toward consecutive_confirmed_regressions or any existing budget counter, or is it always an immediate, separate terminal state?
questions_addressed.answer: It is always an immediate, separate terminal state. Out-of-scope stops do not count toward `consecutive_confirmed_regressions`, iterations, or token budgets.
questions_addressed.justification: A scope breach is an authorization/control failure, not a measured quality regression. Counting it as a regression would let a small number of tolerated regressions mask a critical control failure.
questions_addressed.basis: requirements.md open question 1 leaning; ADR-017 defines regression as a quality-ratchet outcome.

questions_addressed.question: Do we want a dedicated scope_violations list in the progress record / terminal report for observability, or is a single terminal report entry sufficient?
questions_addressed.answer: Yes, add a dedicated `scope_violations` list to the `ProgressRecord` and surface it in the terminal report.
questions_addressed.justification: Scope violations are rare but critical. A structured, durable list supports post-mortems and cross-run observability, mirroring the existing `regression_evidence` and `reverted_proposals` evidence lists in v5.
questions_addressed.basis: requirements.md Requirement 5 (diagnostic payload); vault/services/edd_refinement.md (ProgressRecord v5 evidence lists).

questions_addressed.question: For the Requirement 3 pre-check: should a plan-time scope violation still get recorded as a candidate for get_candidate_status symmetry, even though no edd_do/validate_candidate ran?
questions_addressed.answer: No. A plan-time violation is not a candidate. Record it as a `scope_violations` entry; `get_candidate_status` remains for actual executed candidates.
questions_addressed.justification: `CandidateValidationResult` and `get_candidate_status` describe an executed candidate. Recording a plan-time violation as a candidate would misrepresent the shape and lifecycle of that entity.
questions_addressed.basis: requirements.md Requirement 3; existing `validate_candidate` contract is post-execution.

questions_addressed.question: Should trailing-slash normalization for directory scope entries be enforced at EddRefinementInput parse time or handled defensively in the containment helper?
questions_addressed.answer: `InitializeRunActivity` canonicalizes the scope at run start (POSIX, repo-relative, trailing slash for existing directories). The `PathScopeChecker` uses the trailing slash as the exact-file/directory discriminator and does no filesystem IO itself.
questions_addressed.justification: This makes the persisted scope canonical and resumable, keeps the containment helper pure and deterministic, and still supports the required sibling-prefix rejection semantics.
questions_addressed.basis: requirements.md Requirement 1 and open question 4; common/scoped_path_validator.py path-containment primitive.

questions_addressed.question: Should this work be delivered as two vertical slices (scope persistence + plan-time rejection, then do-time validation + cleanup) or as one cohesive multi-activity change?
questions_addressed.justification: The persistence, plan-time gate, diff-time gate, and terminal cleanup are mutually dependent. Splitting them would leave intermediate states where a violation could be missed or the worktree/lease left dirty.
